newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: DEL MONTE SEEN FOCUSING ON FRUIT JUICE.
newsitem.headline: DEL MONTE SEEN FOCUSING ON FRUIT JUICE.

text.p: A restructuring at South Africa's Del Monte Royal Foods Ltd is expected to focus the firm away from its traditional canned fruits and more towards fruit juices, analysts said on Friday.
Analysts said a trend towards healthy eating in Europe and North America had seen the fruit juice market grow rapidly at the expense of canned fruits -- where the market is more static.

"They will still be able to sell canned fruit in the developing world, but in Europe they (Del Monte) are moving towards fruit juices. I expect them to focus more tightly on that," said SocGen Frankel Pollak analyst John Moses.
Earlier the firm announced that it is to embark on a restructuring process that will include one-off charges and changes to its accounting policy.

"As a result of these issues, a material reduction in earnings is expected at both the interim and year-end stage compared with the equivalent periods of the 1996 financial year," the firm said in a statement.
For the year to November 30, Del Monte posted a headline earnings per share of 50.1 cents from 42.2 cents and a dividend of 19.0 cents from 16 cents.

A company spokesman declined to comment on exactly what the restructuring might contain, saying the process of finalising the details had not yet been concluded. "It is still under discussion," he said.
Analysts said they expected the restructuring to contain few or no disposals, but industry sources said it was possible some minor sales might be on the cards.
"There may be some limited disposals," one source said.

Analysts said the move had not been unexpected, especially after the firm said in February that it was launching a strategic review of its European operations. But they added that the scale of the problems at the firm had caught them by surprise.
Del Monte's share price slid 55 cents to 270 cents by 0853 GMT on Friday as dealers also digested a warning from the firm that its markets had proved tougher than expected.
"The underlying trading of the group has to date been weaker than was anticipated at the time of the release of the year-end November, 1996, results," the firm said.
Analysts said rival fruit and vegetable producer Langeberg Holdings Ltd had given hints things were tougher than usual when it posted half year results in May.

The firm narrowly upped its headline share to 25.5 cents from 23.1 cents, but added that market conditions had become more competitive with satisfactory domestic sales, but a weakening international market.
Del Monte, with a much more significant overseas exposure, is seen as likely to be hit harder by the faltering international market, analysts said.
